articles.title: 'Got to teach that boy': LaMelo Ball responds to Lonzo accusing him of travel on Wolves debut
articles.summary: LaMelo Ball began his Minnesota Timberwolves career in fine fashion by helping them beat the Miami Heat 131-106. Anthony Edwards was the star of the show for...
articles.body:
LaMelo Ball began his Minnesota Timberwolves career in fine fashion by helping them beat the Miami Heat 131-106.

Anthony Edwards was the star of the show for the Wolves, but his combination play with Ball was a sight to behold in their first game together.

While his performance has earned a lot of praise, there has been some controversy too about a non-call from the officials that even LaMelo's own brother, Lonzo, called out.

LaMelo Ball responds to Lonzo's travel accusation during Timberwolves vs Heat

During the first quarter of the game between the Minnesota Timberwolves and Miami Heat, Ball was accused of travelling by many fans.

The point guard used a screen from Rudy Gobert to shed his defender before shuffling back for a three-pointer from the right side of the court.

Although nothing was made of it in real time, replays showed that Ball had taken extra steps after picking up his dribble, which shocked fans and also the commentators, because the officials allowed it.

Even LaMelo's brother, Lonzo, took to X and accused him of a travel, but the new Wolves star was having none of that after the game.

Speaking to ESPN about his brother's tweet, he said: "He's hating. He's hating. See, I've got to give him a call right now. Because with the family, he knows what he's supposed to do: even if I'm wrong, I'm right.

"That's how it goes. I've got to teach that boy!"

LaMelo also defended his move and argued that it wasn't a travel. He said: "If you watch, I let the ball guide. If I let the ball guide and I'm not touching it, you can take as many steps as you want. It's not travel."

The game was won and Ball was fantastic, so he will not care whether that action should've been flagged or not. All that mattered was the win, and the Wolves got it.

articles.title: Backstage WWE and AEW Rumors on Jordynne Grace, The New Level and More
articles.summary: Jordynne Grace has been conspicuously absent from WWE television, and a new report provides the latest update on the former TNA Knockouts champion.
articles.body:
Jordynne Grace has been conspicuously absent from WWE television, and a new report provides the latest update on the former TNA Knockouts champion.

Also in this collection of insider reports is the latest on The New Level's deal with All Elite Wrestling and a shift in perspective within WWE Creative.

Sean Ross Sapp reported on Fightful's The Hump (20:35) that vignettes were filmed this past summer for a proposed tag team pairing Jordynne Grace with Ivy Nile, to be known as "Iron Built." The tentative plan was for the pair to return to television in late September.

He noted that he "has not heard anything else about them coming back to TV."

Sapp also reported that Grace is signed through 2029 and did not receive a new deal when she moved to the main roster because her original contract already paid above the main roster minimum, as Joe Hendry's did.

Grace recently competed in a fitness competition, but she has been off television since losing to Kiana James on the June 18 episode of Main Event and has not appeared on SmackDown since April 17, when she lost a Women's United States Championship No. 1 Contender's match to Tiffany Stratton.

Grace has been woefully underutilized, despite proving her excellence during her run in TNA, where she was a top competitor in the Knockouts division, one of its most decorated wrestlers and involved in some of that roster's greatest matches.

It remains to be seen whether that tag team with Nile will materialize or if it will be back to the drawing board. For now, Grace's usage in WWE has been a glaring negative for the creative team.

The New Level is All Elite for the foreseeable future.

Sapp reported to Fightful Select that "Austin Creed and Kofi are under five-year contracts with AEW. In addition, the creative was pitched to them well before a deal was nailed down, and the trio with Swerve was one of the opening ideas given to them."

He added: "New Level lost the Trios titles this past week, which we're told was never meant to be a long-term run."

Austin Creed and Kofi worked with Swerve Strickland because he was a huge part of "bridging the relationship" between All Elite Wrestling and The New Level, since "Tony Khan wouldn't speak with them until they were contractually free."

One of the greatest, most decorated tag teams of all time, The New Level arrived in AEW with plenty to prove after a lackluster conclusion to their WWE run saw them undergo a heel turn that the creative team fumbled harder than a running back on a rainy day before becoming an afterthought on Monday nights.

Now, with an opportunity to prove they have plenty left between the ropes and from a character standpoint, Creed and Kofi have (at least) five years to rewrite the narrative of the back half of their pro wrestling careers.

Dave Meltzer reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that WWE is seriously reconsidering how it presents Mexican wrestlers following the success of the Penta-Roman Reigns matchup on the September 14 episode of Raw.

It is not difficult to see why, though it is something the company should have been taking under consideration long before that.

Penta has been over at a main event-worthy level since he arrived in the company and has checked every box since. That the fans in Mexico were so red hot and ready to see him win the World Heavyweight Championship was just the latest indicator that there is plenty for the luchadors from Mexico to offer the current-day WWE product.

Look no further than the acclaim AAA has earned under the WWE umbrella. Mark Calaway (The Undertaker) and Jeremy Borash have helped deliver a tremendous product featuring some of the best work across WWE's brands, including an all-time classic Mask vs. Mask match between El Grande Americano and The Original El Grande Americano.

Recently, Dragon Lee has seen his star shine brighter than before, thanks to a series of matches with Chad Gable and a couple of big wins in singles competition.

Hopefully, this is just the beginning of the doors opening for Mexican talent in WWE, where they will have the opportunity to steal shows and become even bigger stars.

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Sheetal Devi's double gold, Shailesh Kumar-led podium sweep headline India's best day yet
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed its best day at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Thursday, winning 26 medals, including seven golds, as a remarkable medal rush
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed its best day at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Thursday, winning 26 medals, including seven golds, as a remarkable medal rush across athletics, archery, swimming, badminton and table tennis took the country's overall tally to 88.Armless archer Sheetal Devi led the charge with two gold medals in less than two hours, while the track-and-field contingent remained India's biggest contributor. Suvarna Raj, Shailesh Kumar, Anjanaben Bumbadiya, Dilip Mahadu Gavit and Solairaj Dharmaraj were among the other gold medallists on a memorable day for the Indian contingent.India's tally now stands at 21 gold, 26 silver and 41 bronze medals. The seven golds helped the country reclaim fourth place in the standings after it slipped to sixth on Day 2 and fifth on Day 3.Sheetal Devi strikes twice, Swati Chaudhary makes historySheetal, the 19-year-old reigning world champion and world No. 1, began her golden run by teaming up with Toman Kumar to defend India's mixed team title. The Indian duo beat Indonesia's Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148.Less than two hours later, Sheetal returned to the range for the women's individual final. After overcoming a four-point deficit, she defeated Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah 142-139 to repeat her triumph from the Hangzhou 2023 Asian Para Games.India also celebrated a historic achievement in archery as Swati Chaudhary won the country's first-ever Asian Para Games medal in the W1 category. She settled for silver after losing 4-6 to China's Cen Mengkan in the women's individual final.ALSO READ: Where India stands in medal tally after best day with 26 medals, including 7 goldsAthletics powers India's seven-gold haulThe day began with Suvarna Raj winning gold in the women's F54 discus throw with a best effort of 15.66m. The 44-year-old wheelchair athlete recorded four throws beyond 15 metres to secure the biggest win of her career.India then enjoyed a podium sweep in the men's high jump T63 event. Shailesh Kumar, who had won bronze in the long jump on Wednesday, led the way with a Games-record effort of 1.89m. Former Paralympic bronze medallist Varun Bhati took silver with a season's best of 1.84m, while Rahul completed the all-Indian podium with a jump of 1.81m.Anjanaben Bumbadiya won the women's 400m T47 gold in 59.97 seconds, with compatriot Jayanti Behera taking silver in 1:00.65. Dilip Mahadu Gavit, who had won the men's 100m T47 gold on Wednesday, added another title by winning the men's 400m T47 final in 48.27 seconds.Solairaj Dharmaraj provided a fitting finish to the day's athletics action, successfully defending his men's long jump T44/T62/T64 title with an Asian-record effort of 7.15m. Malaysia's Eddy Bernard won silver with 6.34m, while Japan's Yuma Tamaki took bronze with a personal-best 6.89m.Tejalben Damor also added to India's medal count, winning silver in the women's 400m T12 in 57.60 seconds. The visually impaired athlete had earlier claimed bronze in the 200m T12 event.Four more swimming medals, Ravi Budigina completes hat-trickIndia added four medals in the pool, taking its overall swimming haul to 10, although a gold remained elusive.Eighteen-year-old Ravi Budigina secured bronze in the men's 50m freestyle S13 with a time of 25.89 seconds. It was his third medal of the Games, following silver-medal finishes in the 100m backstroke and freestyle events.Kapil Kumar won silver in the men's 400m freestyle S10 in 4:38.44, finishing behind Japan's Akito Minai, who set a Games record of 4:27.44. Swatik Patil claimed bronze in the men's 100m breaststroke SB9 in 1:13.77, while Tejas Nandakumar took bronze in the men's 100m backstroke S7 with a time of 1:18.58.Indian shuttlers assured of multiple badminton medalsIndia's para-shuttlers also enjoyed a productive day, with Pramod Bhagat and Nitesh Kumar setting up an all-Indian men's singles SL3 final.Six-time world champion and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Bhagat survived a marathon two-hour-and-nine-minute semifinal against South Korea's Lee Seunghu, winning 16-21, 21-18, 21-17.Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh had earlier defeated Indonesia's M Imran 21-19, 21-16 to reach the final. He also advanced to the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final with Thulasimathi Murugesan after the Indian pair beat China's Li Mingpin and Xiao Zuxian 21-19, 14-21, 21-17.Naveen Sivakumar reached the men's singles SL4 final, while Indian shuttlers collected five bronze medals across other events.Bhavina Patel, Subham Wadhwa win table tennis bronzeIndia's medal rush extended to para-table tennis, where Bhavina Patel and Subham Wadhwa secured bronze in mixed doubles XD7.The Indian pair lost 6-11, 11-8, 5-11, 8-11 to South Korea's Jang Yeongjin and Lee Migyu in the semifinals after beating Japan's Kimie Bessho and Masanori Uno 11-9, 11-3, 11-6 in the quarterfinals.China continued to dominate the overall standings, crossing 300 medals to reach 313, including 149 golds. Hosts Japan were second with 136 medals, including 40 gold, while Uzbekistan occupied third place with 117 medals, including 37 gold.India's seven-gold day lifted the contingent back to fourth place, with 88 medals overall and momentum building across multiple disciplines.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor McDavid’s mother Kelly: How her sacrifices and support helped the Edmonton Oilers star and his brother Cameron pursue their hockey dreams
articles.summary: Discover the pivotal role Kelly McDavid played in guiding Connor McDavid and his brother Cameron through their hockey aspirations, emphasizing family support, sacrifice, and balance in their lives.
articles.body: Connor McDavid’s rise as one of the NHL’s elite players started long before the spotlight turned to him in Edmonton, and growing up in Newmarket, Ontario, he developed his hockey skills with the help of his parents, Kelly and Brian McDavid, and his older brother, Cameron. The family’s dedication went further than practices and games, with schoolwork, health and everyday family life still important parts of the journey.It wasn't just about bringing a future superstar to the NHL, though. She also had to support two sons with their own goals, juggle the demands of youth hockey and help them navigate the pressures that came with competing at a high level. In interviews about the family’s hockey years, Kelly has spoken about the time, effort and sacrifices made to keep both boys involved in the sport.How Kelly McDavid supports Connor McDavid beyond NHLKelly McDavid’s involvement in Connor’s development was far more than just standing in the stands and cheering. She helped to create a family setting where his ambitions could blossom, and his well-being was paramount. As Connor’s remarkable talent became apparent, the challenge was to nurture his drive while preventing hockey from taking over every part of his childhood.Connor started organized hockey at a young age and was excited to play against older kids. Kelly remembered wanting to move up in the sport. But also understood the pressure of being younger than most of his competitors, and her response was to talk over his goals with him and help him take the next step in manageable steps.An example of that approach was when Connor wanted to get to a higher level of minor hockey. Instead of viewing the ambition as a demand of the moment, Kelly helped him focus on the games ahead and the progress needed to achieve his target. It was a case study in how practical encouragement could help a motivated young athlete without making success seem like an all-or-nothing proposition.Kelly also paid attention to the mundane details of raising a young hockey player. The regime involved eating properly, getting enough sleep, doing schoolwork and recognizing when you were tired. In her account of the family’s minor-hockey years, she portrayed herself as the caregiver who worried about the boys’ health and whether the schedule was getting too busy.As Connor’s reputation grew, that balance was key. The opportunities grew, the chance to master the game grew, and the expectations grew, even as the family struggled to maintain some normalcy. Kelly’s support was a timely reminder that elite athletes often need people who take care of the practicalities and offer reassurance when they are off the rink.Connor McDavid’s childhood, family values and hockey journeyBoth Connor and Cameron grew up playing hockey, but they didn’t have the same path. Cameron, the older brother, was already practicing and playing before Connor was old enough to play with him. Connor was keen to be involved, and the competitive sporting environment they shared helped fuel his competitive nature. Their father, Brian, was also heavily involved in hockey, coaching and being there to support the boys through the demands of their respective teams.The family’s planning involved coordination and personal sacrifice. When the boys were both playing, Brian spent more time with Connor and coached him, while Kelly took care of Cameron’s hockey schedule. The parents split their attention between the brothers and tried to make the best of the time they could have together as a family, Kelly said. Their approach acknowledged that both sons needed support, even when their schedules and needs didn’t always align.There was also the commitment of long days, travel and balancing school with sport. Kelly remembers the tournament schedule meant the kids missed school and the family still had expectations around homework. If the boys wanted to continue playing hockey, they had to keep up with their schoolwork. Kelly helped them manage their time, but part of the family’s approach was still to stay on top of schoolwork.Encouragement was also needed on Cameron’s path. Kelly said he worked to build a higher-level team and needed support when the gains didn’t come right away. His experience showed the family's hockey journey was about more than just Connor's ascent.The brothers each had their own goals, and their parents wanted to help them stick with it through setbacks.Kelly’s sacrifices were part of a larger commitment to give both boys a chance to play the game they loved. She’s talked about the time and effort that goes into getting your kids to play hockey at a high level, but also the relationships and experiences that made those years meaningful.How Connor McDavid’s family helps him handle pressureEven before he began his professional career, Connor felt the pressure of being labeled a generational hockey talent. He competed many times against older opponents, and he had to cope with expectations that were strange for his age. Kelly’s approach was to keep the lines of communication open, to encourage him to keep his feet on the ground, and to remind him that he was more than just his performance on the ice.That support was especially important as Connor left home to play junior hockey with the Erie Otters in Pennsylvania. The move was a step into the professional hockey ranks and an adjustment to life outside the family home. His parents had to balance their instinct to care for him with the need to allow him to become more independent. The family has been reported as a central source of stability during this period in his early career.Kelly, too, had to deal with the attention her son brought. Connor's rising profile drew more public attention to his work and personal life. In a 2017 interview, she talked about life as the mother of a hockey phenomenon, reflecting on the weirdness that comes with having a child become a huge figure in the sport.The family’s emphasis on humility and perspective kept things in perspective. Kelly has described Connor as someone who didn’t like being the center of attention and knew how important teammates were. Her advice was not to temper his ambition; it was to help him cope with success and adversity without forgetting the people around him.Family ties continue to be part of Connor’s life as he takes on the responsibility of captaining the Edmonton Oilers. In a 2026 first-person account, he made a humorous observation about his transition from living at home to being a captain in the NHL, noting that his mother still took care of things for him on a daily basis. The anecdote was a fine illustration of the difference between his public role as the head of the team and his place in the family.Maybe it’s these mundane acts of support that better show the scope of Kelly’s influence than any one moment. She helped navigate the practicalities of hockey, supported both boys through their individual struggles and created space for family life in the midst of a busy schedule. Her role was not to control the outcome, but to give the brothers a solid foundation to follow their goals.But Connor’s success with the Edmonton Oilers has made him one of hockey’s most recognizable stars, and that journey began with years of family involvement and shared sacrifice. Cameron's own trip was also part of it, requiring time, encouragement and attention from both parents. articles.title: Ron Duguay Dies at Age 69, Rangers Legend Played in 1979 Stanley Cup Final
articles.summary: Ron Duguay, a 12-year NHL veteran, has died at the age of 69.
articles.body:
Ron Duguay, a 12-year NHL veteran, has died at the age of 69.

The New York Rangers, Duguay's team for eight of his 12 seasons, issued a statement on Thursday morning.

Duguay revealed in February that had he was diagnosed with Stage 4 cancer that originated in his colon more than one year earlier.

Shay Thomas, Duguay's daughter, wrote an Instagram post in July revealing the cancer had spread to his liver and he was recovering after fainting at home due to extreme dehydration.

"It's with a shattered heart but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now," former Alaska governor Sarah Palin, who was dating Duguay, said on social media . "He fought so hard. Love never ends."

Duguay was selected with the No. 13 overall pick by the Rangers in the 1977 NHL amateur draft. He appeared in 70 games as a rookie, finishing with 40 points.

The Rangers made a run to the Stanley Cup Final during Duguay's second season in 1978-79. He had five goals and four assists in 18 appearances during that postseason run.

New York lost in the final to the Montreal Canadiens in five games. It was the franchise's first time reaching the Stanley Cup Final since 1972.

Duguay spent his first six seasons with the Rangers before being traded to the Detroit Red Wings before the 1983-84 campaign. He spent more than two seasons in Detroit, then was traded in 1986 to the Pittsburgh Penguins.

The Penguins subsequently traded Duguay back to the Rangers in January 1987. He remained with the club for parts of two seasons before joining the Los Angeles Kings late in the 1987-88 season.

Duguay finished his career with the Kings before retiring after the 1988-89 campaign. He racked up 274 goals and 346 assists in 864 games with four different teams.

articles.title: India resist New Zealand fightback to win record-setting T20 cricket opener
articles.summary: New Zealand reach their highest home total against India, 225-4, but Sanju Samson hits fifty to top the record in chase.
articles.body:
India overcame a spirited New Zealand fightback after a blazing start to secure a thrilling four-wicket victory in Christchurch ⁠on Thursday and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match T20 series.

India survived a mid-innings wobble in a 226-run chase after openers Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma laid the platform, with Shreyas Iyer’s ⁠contribution reviving the chase and Naman Dhir applying the finishing touches to seal victory in 19.4 overs.

“When they [the openers] click, they set up the game for us, and the rest of us try to steady the ship and finish,” India captain Iyer said. “He [Dhir] gives us lots of options. I personally feel the calm and composed ‌nature he showed tonight, it was magnificent.”

Put in to bat, New Zealand made the most of favourable conditions as openers Tim Seifert and Finn Allen set the tone before Glenn Phillips produced a dazzling knock to propel the hosts to 225-4.

The total was New Zealand’s biggest T20 score against India on home soil, but the visitors completed their highest-ever successful run chase despite a stuttering middle phase.

Samson and Abhishek stitched together a 93-run opening stand, with Samson hammering 67 off 33 ⁠balls, including eight fours and four sixes, as India surged to 94-1 in ⁠the powerplay.

New Zealand hit back by removing three batters in quick succession, but Iyer countered with 42 off 28 balls to wrest back the momentum, before a late flourish from Dhir (42 not out) took India over the line.

“They [Indian openers] put us under ⁠pressure. Another big powerplay from them. We were not at our best,” New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said.

“In the middle, we did well to squeeze ⁠them. Tight game and both teams might look at things that ⁠could have gone here or there.”

Seifert and Allen had earlier given New Zealand a solid platform, helping the hosts reach 65-1 in the powerplay, with Allen blasting 45 off 24 balls.

Phillips then took charge, producing an unbeaten 82 off 40 deliveries, including eight ‌fours and three sixes, while Bevon Jacobs added 31 before being run out.

India’s bowlers struggled to contain the scoring, with all five used going at 10 runs an over or more.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar, playing his ‌first ‌T20 international in four years after last featuring against New Zealand in 2022, endured an expensive return with figures of 0-49.

The second T20 will be played on Saturday in Christchurch.

articles.title: Luke Humphries withdraws from European Championship
articles.summary: World number two Luke Humphries pulls out of the European Championship because of gastroenteritis.
articles.body:
World number two Luke Humphries has pulled out of the European Championship in Germany because of gastroenteritis.

Humphries was coming into the tournament on the back of winning the World Grand Prix prior to reaching the final of the Swiss Darts Trophy final, which he lost to Jonny Clayton.

Kim Huybrechts will come in as a replacement as the Belgian is the highest-ranked player from the 2026 European Tour rankings who had not qualified.

Huybrechts will face Ryan Searle when the European Championship starts in Dortmund on Thursday, while Gerwyn Price will play Rob Cross and defending champion Gian van Veen will take on Andrew Gilding among the night's eight matches.

World number one and PDC world champion Luke Littler will start his challenge on Friday with a match against William O'Connor.

articles.summary: Tonybet te ofrece las mejores cuotas para el Gran Premio de Estados Unidos
articles.body: El Gran Premio de Estados Unidos, que se corre el domingo 25 de octubre, es para Fernando Alonso una oportunidad de redimir un curso que no tiene nada que ver con lo que prometía el fichaje de Adrian Newey y el estreno del motor Honda. Hablar de una temporada regular sería generoso. Alonso llega a Texas con siete puntos, 17º en el Mundial, mientras Aston Martin ocupa el último puesto entre los constructores. Solo ha puntuado tres veces, con un décimo puesto en Mónaco, un noveno en Zandvoort y un octavo en Sepang, y se ha quedado tirado hasta en seis ocasiones por la fiabilidad de la unidad japonesa. Ese octavo puesto de Malasia, el mejor resultado del equipo en 2026, llegó en una carrera caótica y fue más un oasis que un cambio de tendencia. El último capítulo no invita al optimismo. En Singapur tuvo que salir desde el pit-lane tras cambios en el motor y terminó sin puntos. Honda admitió después que el resultado reflejaba el nivel real del equipo. El propio Alonso llegó a calificar la unidad de "ridícula". Son malas noticias en una pista de largas rectas y fuertes aceleraciones, justo donde la entrega de potencia se paga más cara. Ahí entra el mercado de las casas de apuestas. Tonybet paga a 7.00 que Alonso termine entre los diez primeros. Es una cuota alta, pero no disparatada para un piloto que ha cruzado la meta en zona de puntos en tres de las 17 carreras. El problema es que esas tres actuaciones llegaron en circuitos más amables y con carreras revueltas. El año pasado, en este mismo escenario, acabó décimo y sumó dos puntos. Repetir ese guion sería un éxito, y la veteranía del asturiano en una carrera caótica es su principal aval. La otra cara de la moneda de las apuestas deportivas es la cuota de 34.00 a que acabe entre los seis primeros. Su mejor puesto este año es un octavo, y para soñar con el top 6 tendría que superar a coches que hoy le sacan casi tres segundos por vuelta en clasificación. Hablamos de una apuesta de pura lotería, reservada para escenarios extremos como una lluvia torrencial, varios safety cars o una cadena de abandonos que dejara la carrera patas arriba. Arriba, la historia es muy distinta. Max Verstappen es el gran favorito, con una cuota de 2.10 para ganar. articles.title: Red Wings Reportedly Reject Key Player in Dylan Larkin Trade Talks
articles.summary: Frank Seravalli reveals why the Red Wings have concerns about Danila Yurov as a centerpiece in potential Dylan Larkin trade talks with Minnesota.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings reportedly have a problem with what the Minnesota Wild are offering in a potential Dylan Larkin trade , and NHL insider Frank Seravalli has revealed the player at the center of the disagreement. According to Seravalli, Detroit isn't convinced that 22-year-old forward Danila Yurov is good enough to serve as one of the primary pieces in a deal involving its former captain.

That is a significant development in a trade saga that has dominated the Red Wings' offseason and continued into October. Minnesota has been considered one of Larkin's preferred destinations, but apparently finding common ground on a return package has been easier said than done.

Red Wings Reportedly Balk at Danila Yurov in Dylan Larkin Trade Talks

During a Tuesday appearance on Flames Now , Seravalli provided insight into the discussions between Detroit and Minnesota. His comments suggest that the Red Wings have reservations about the quality of the young player the Wild could build their offer around.

"I think in trade talks, the Red Wings have balked a little bit about the quality of Danila Yurov being one of the centerpieces," Seravalli said .

That is not the same as Detroit formally rejecting a completed trade offer, but it does reveal an important sticking point. The Red Wings apparently aren't convinced that Yurov represents the caliber of young talent they should demand when discussing a player of Larkin's importance.

Yurov was selected 24th overall in the 2022 NHL Draft and recorded 27 points in 73 games during his rookie season. He has started the 2026-27 campaign with five points in his first 10 games, showing signs of improvement while continuing to develop his offensive game.

Still, Detroit would be surrendering a proven top-line center who has scored at least 30 goals in five consecutive seasons. That makes it understandable why interim general manager Shawn Horcoff would be reluctant to accept a package built primarily around a player who has yet to establish himself as a consistent top-six NHL forward.

Detroit's Asking Price Remains Extremely High

The reported disagreement becomes even more interesting when considering what the Red Wings are believed to want in exchange for Larkin. NHL insider Darren Dreger has indicated that Detroit's asking price includes multiple premium assets rather than one promising young player.

According to Dreger's reported trade framework , the Red Wings have been looking for two high-end prospects, an established top-nine NHL forward, and a first-round draft pick. That would represent a significant investment for Minnesota, especially considering the organization's existing salary-cap commitments.

For Detroit, however, the demand makes sense when considering what losing Larkin would mean to the lineup. The Red Wings are already searching for additional scoring and center depth, and moving their most established center without receiving immediate help could make those problems even worse.

As we previously reported , former general manager Steve Yzerman warned that moving Larkin for primarily future assets would likely leave Detroit worse in the short term. That concern remains relevant because the organization is attempting to become competitive rather than begin another lengthy rebuild.

The Wild have an obvious reason to pursue Larkin, and it goes beyond adding another productive center. Minnesota already has an impressive collection of offensive talent, and pairing Larkin with players such as Kirill Kaprizov could make the organization even more dangerous.

There is also the Quinn Hughes factor to consider, as Minnesota is working toward securing the defenseman's long-term future. Larkin and Hughes have a relationship through international hockey, and speculation has suggested that acquiring Larkin could strengthen Minnesota's position as it attempts to convince Hughes to sign an extension.

However, Minnesota must determine how much of its future it is willing to sacrifice for a 30-year-old center. Yurov is still developing, and giving up additional prospects and first-round selections could create problems for the Wild several seasons down the road.

Meanwhile, Detroit has very little reason to make a deal simply for the sake of ending the ongoing speculation. Larkin remains under contract through the 2030-31 season, carrying an annual salary-cap hit of $8.7 million.

The timing of Seravalli's comments is especially interesting because speculation about an approaching trade has intensified over the past week. As we recently reported , ESPN's John Buccigross suggested that a Larkin trade could happen within seven to 10 days of his October 16 comments.

Whether that prediction proves accurate remains to be seen, but the reported disagreement involving Yurov provides a possible explanation for why Minnesota hasn't completed a deal. The Wild appear interested in acquiring Larkin, while Detroit remains determined to receive a return that reflects his established value.

Seravalli's comments do not establish that the Red Wings have turned down a formal offer or ended negotiations with Minnesota. They do, however, suggest Horcoff isn't prepared to settle for a prospect-driven package unless the quality of the assets meets Detroit's expectations.

If Minnesota wants to acquire Larkin, it may have to strengthen its offer considerably. Otherwise, the Red Wings can continue evaluating other potential destinations while keeping one of their most important players in Detroit.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith believes Titans' John Franklin-Myers is the 'true hero'
articles.summary: Stephen A. Smith calls Titans' John Franklin-Myers a hero for his role in de-escalating the recent Jordan Elliott incident.
articles.body:
After the Jordan Elliott news broke at the Tennessee Titans facility on Wednesday, the media landscape has been differing views on the incident and how Robert Saleh and the organization handled it.

While these takes mostly center on Saleh and Elliott, with comments spanning the emotional spectrum, one aspect of the story has largely flown under the radar: John Franklin-Myers's role in de-escalating the situation.

This situation was ugly, and it truly could have cascaded into a nightmare that would have left a tragic imprint on the organization if not for Franklin-Myers, who, as Stephen A. Smith points out, is the true hero.

"And I just want to say that when I think of that defensive lineman, John Franklin-Myers. You don't throw these words around too easily, too often, but if there is a hero in all of this, it is him," he said.

In that moment, Franklin-Myers took leadership to a new level, proving he was worth every penny of the offseason contract he signed, and that he is a true leader of men and, like Smith said, a hero.

articles.title: Ron Duguay, part of the 1980s Detroit Red Wings revival, dies at 69
articles.summary: Ron Duguay played for Detroit Red Wings from 1983-86 and spent 8 seasons with New York Rangers (1977-83, 1986-88). He died on Thursday, Oct. 22.
articles.body:
Ron Duguay , who enjoyed a career revival during his stint with the Detroit Red Wings , has died after a battle with cancer.

He passed away aged 69 on Thursday, Oct. 22.

Duguay, from Sudbury, Ontario, played eight seasons with the New York Rangers (1977-83, 1986-88), but was on a career decline when the Wings acquired in a trade on June 13, 1983. The Wings sent Willie Huber, Mark Osborne, and Mike Blaisdell to the Rangers for Duguay (along with Eddie Mio and Ed Johnstone.

Duguay appealed as part of the revival in the early 1980s under then-general manager Jimmy Devellano, who was the first hire made by Mike and Marian Ilitch after buying the team from Bruce Norris in 1982. The following year, Devellano drafted Steve Yzerman at No. 4 , beginning the revival of the franchise. ( Devellano remains in the Wings' front office .)

In 1983-84, Duguay was fourth on the Wings with 33 goals , and fourth on the team with 47 assists, and third with 80 points. The following season he ranked second with 38 goals, 51 assists and 89 points, the latter two career highs.

At the 1986 trade deadline, the Wings sent Duguay to the Pittsburgh Penguins for Doug Shedden. Duguay also played for the Pittsburgh Penguins and Los Angeles Kings .

He had 620 points (274 goals, 346 assists) in 864 regular-season career games and 53 points (31 goals, 22 assists) in 89 Stanley Cup Playoff games.

"Ron lived life with an extraordinary passion, an infectious smile, and a heart that was truly larger than life," the NHL Alumni Association said in a social media post. "Above all else, his deepest and most sincere love was for his family. They were his greatest pride, his greatest joy, and always closest to his heart.

"His dedication and passion for the game of hockey were unwavering. Hockey was more than a sport to Ron; it was a part of who he was, a lifelong love that he carried with pride and shared so generously with others. But perhaps what made Ron most special was his humanity. His genuine compassion, kindness, and willingness to help others always extended far beyond himself. He cared deeply, gave generously of his heart, and had a remarkable way of making everyone around him feel valued and appreciated."

articles.title: Lamar Jackson returns to Ravens practice ahead of Bengals matchup
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson was present at the start of Thursday’s practice, another encouraging step as Baltimore prepares to host Cincinnati
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson returned to the field for Thursday's practice, giving the Ravens another encouraging development ahead of Sunday's matchup against Cincinnati. Jamison Hensley and Brian Wacker reported Jackson's presence during the opening portion available to reporters. It marked a significant step after the quarterback missed that portion Wednesday before getting limited work later.

Jackson was officially listed as limited Wednesday with the ankle injury he suffered against Tennessee on Oct. 4. Thursday's appearance builds on that progress, although his participation level and availability against the Bengals remain to be determined. Before the injury, Jackson completed 68 of 96 passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, producing a 119.6 passer rating. He also rushed for 144 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries, averaging 7.6 yards per attempt.

Baltimore has gone 1-1 in his absence, beating Atlanta in overtime before falling 13-10 at Cleveland. Tyler Huntley completed 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against the Browns, but the Ravens went scoreless over the final three quarters.

Jackson's return would add a different dimension to an offense seeking more consistency. His 10.1 yards per pass attempt this season reflects the explosive passing production Baltimore had before his injury.

The Ravens host a rested Bengals team Sunday with another important division result at stake. Thursday's official injury report and Jackson's response to the increased workload will clarify whether he can make his first appearance since Week 4.

articles.title: Analyzing J.J. McCarthy's initial Giants performance and possible impact against Texans
articles.summary: The Giants are turning to quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who will get the start in Week 7 against the Texans.
articles.body:
Giants head coach John Harbaugh made it official at practice on Wednesday: J.J. McCarthy will start in Houston on Sunday .

After his spectacular comeback bid against the New Orleans Saints in Week 5, what did we learn about how McCarthy fits in with the Giants, and what we can expect from him against the Texans?

Let's break down the key plays in McCarthy's performance...

4th quarter, 10:27 to go – 3rd and 10 at the Saints' 44, Giants trailing 34-10

It's easily forgotten in the hype surrounding his overall performance, but McCarthy actually didn't get off to such a great start. While his first pass - a dump-off to Devin Singletary - went for 19 yards into Saints territory, McCarthy's next two were off the mark, leaving him facing a 3rd-and-long.

On a quick pass underneath, McCarthy threw behind an open Malachi Fields and was intercepted by Martin Emerson Jr. On the play, Fields ran an inside-out route and broke back to the outside right as McCarthy was releasing the pass to him underneath.

This was more of a case of two players not being on the same page due to a lack of chemistry than being anyone's fault. It's still relevant, though, because it's not going to be easy to develop that chemistry overnight. So we can perhaps expect further mistakes of this nature due to communication issues.

4th quarter, 8:24 to go – 1st and 10 at the Saints' 40, Giants trailing 34-10

New Orleans fumbled the ball back to the Giants two plays after Emerson's interception, and McCarthy capitalized with a drive that culminated in Tyrone Tracy 's five-yard touchdown run.

McCarthy's second completion of the game was the one that really seemed to get him going, as Malik Naber s ran a deep over route and McCarthy let rip with a throw down the seam that Nabers hauled in with a leaping grab for 27 yards.

The receivers really stepped up for McCarthy in this game, feeding off the energy of the crowd as he started to get in rhythm. There were a handful of leaping or diving catches, and Isaiah Likely made a one-handed snag on the two-point conversion after the Tracy score.

4th quarter, 5:54 to go – 1st and 10 at the Giants' 27, New York trailing 34-18

McCarthy had plenty of time here, as the Saints sent a four-man rush and one of the four ended up on the ground. He once again uncorked a deep throw, but this time it was underthrown.

On this occasion, McCarthy was the beneficiary of some serious good fortune. The ball rattled out of the hands of the New Orleans defensive back and bobbled up into the air, where Charlie Jones came down with it for a 49-yard gain.

He was lucky again on the next play as Emerson jumped the route on the outside for an apparent interception, only for McCarthy to be spared by the replay booth.

Even the most optimistic Giants fan would have to accept that McCarthy is likely to make some mistakes and may need the bounces to go in his favor at times.

4th quarter, 5:11 to go – 2nd and 10 at the Saints' 24, Giants trailing 34-18

On the very next play after his reprieve from the replay booth, McCarthy connected with Likely in the end zone as he ran down the seam and went up high for another leaping catch. Here you can easily see McCarthy's growing confidence in his teammates' ability to make a play for him if he puts the ball in a spot where they can get after it.

Crucially, though, his throw to Nabers on the two-point conversion that would have made it a one-score game was too high.

McCarthy continued to be in rhythm on his next drive, mostly taking advantage of what the defense was giving him underneath. But he also mixed in another deep connection with Nabers to set up a quick field goal to bring them within seven and give them time to get the ball back.

4th quarter, 40 seconds to go – 2nd and 10 at the Saints' 43, Giants trailing 34-27

McCarthy opened this drive with a long scramble, then made his best throw of the day to take the Giants to the edge of the red zone with 30 seconds remaining.

This was an incredibly tight window throw to Likely on a deep over route, ripped just over the head of a leaping linebacker but in front of two defensive backs. That's the type of throw that will have Giants coaches optimistic that McCarthy can live up to his draft position after all.

From there, the Giants ultimately ran out of time, as they had to spike the ball on first and third down when Nabers' second down catch was just short of the marker. This limited them to one fourth down shot at the end zone that was incomplete.

McCarthy got into a nice rhythm in this game, and his team was clearly energized as he gave them a spark. Some of that was attributable to the Saints playing their safeties deep and trying to keep everything in front of them, but he still deserves credit for changing the momentum with his performance.

With that said, he was in a position where he didn't have anything to lose, so he was able to take a lot of chances that the Giants may be reluctant for him to take in Sunday's game -- so he may end up in more of a game manager role.

Nevertheless, McCarthy's run threat, ability to command the huddle, and success with downfield throws are all positive signs that will give him and his coaches confidence heading into Week 7.

The challenge should not be underestimated, though, because - after an 0-4 start - the Texans have won two straight in impressive fashion and DeMeco Ryans has the defense playing really well. McCarthy wasn't impressive in his 10 starts last season, but the Vikings did win six of them. So if he can lead New York to a win on Sunday, the rest of the season could get very interesting.

articles.title: Arteta says Wenger made it possible for him to coach Arsenal
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has revealed the role that Arsene Wenger played in him becoming the manager of Arsenal, a role he has occupied since the end of 2019. The former...
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has revealed the role that Arsene Wenger played in him becoming the manager of Arsenal, a role he has occupied since the end of 2019. The former midfielder came back to Arsenal three years after he left the club and ended his playing career before joining Manchester City as the assistant coach to Pep Guardiola.

Arteta has become one of the best coaches in the game and won the first Arsenal league title in 22 years . Arsenal remains one of the top clubs in the world, and there is no doubt that the Gunners have what it takes to win more trophies this season and in the campaigns ahead.

Arteta's former teammates all say that he already showed them, as a player, that he would become a manager and a top one at that, and the ex-midfielder has now opened up about being inspired by Wenger to become an Arsenal coach. He said via TNT Sports :

"Well, huge. I would not be sitting here if it was not for Arsene. First of all, the opportunities that he gave me to be a part of this incredible football club.

"Everything that I learnt from him about values and about how somebody at that level has to behave, has to treat people and has to operate. The level of honesty and loyalty that he always showed towards everybody, and then his philosophy about the game and how it has to be played: the roles of the players and how you want to feel when you enter that field."

Arteta's words show the deep respect he has for Wenger, and the influence of the Frenchman is clear in the way the Spaniard has built his team. The values and philosophy that Wenger instilled continue to shape the club's identity.

The Gunners' success under Arteta is a testament to the foundation laid by Wenger, and the current manager has built on that legacy. The club's ambition remains high, and the fans will hope for more silverware.

Arteta's journey from player to manager is a story of continuity, and Wenger's role in that journey cannot be overstated. The bond between the two is clear, and the club's future looks bright.

articles.title: Kevin Durant says everything you need to know about how Fred VanVleet changes everything for Rockets
articles.summary: The Houston Rockets finally have Fred VanVleet back running their offense, and Kevin Durant believes the veteran point guard’s return changes how effectivel...
articles.body:
The Houston Rockets finally have Fred VanVleet back running their offense, and Kevin Durant believes the veteran point guard's return changes how effectively everyone on the roster can play their natural roles.

Houston opened the 2026-27 season Wednesday night with a convincing 128-110 win over the Dallas Mavericks . Afterward, Durant explained how the Rockets' improved backcourt spacing and playmaking already differ from last season.

Durant spoke during his postgame news conference in a video shared by Chris Baldwin of PaperCity Magazine via X, formerly known as Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Last year we started in our backcourt, Twin (Amen Thompson) and Josh Okogie. And a lot of time those guys are being left at the 3-point line. And their men are helping guard guys in the paint. So when we've got Fred and Marcus Smart out there who can keep the defense honest at the 3-point line and then Twin just roaming around just doing everything. Grabbing offensive rebounds, making assists, dunks, floaters, everything."

Durant said having VanVleet and Smart handling traditional guard responsibilities allows Houston's other players to settle into more favorable roles.

"That put everybody into a good position. That settle everybody into what they do best. You've seen how efficient Alpe (Sengun) was tonight. Bari (Smith Jr.). Everybody's just more efficient when they're just in their roles, doing what they do.

"Everybody had to play point guard by committee last year. And I think having a few natural point guards on our team, that's going to help everybody."

Fred VanVleet's return unlocks Rockets' offense in season-opening win

VanVleet showed that impact immediately in his first regular-season game back from the torn ACL that sidelined him throughout last season. He finished with six points and 11 assists without committing a turnover across 30 minutes. He also recorded three steals while shooting 2-for-8 from the field and 2-for-6 from 3-point range.

Meanwhile, Houston's primary scorers thrived.

Durant opened Year 20 with 30 points, six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. He shot 10-for-16 from the field, 2-for-4 from beyond the arc and 8-for-11 at the free-throw line in 37 minutes.

Jabari Smith Jr. matched Durant with 30 points on 11-for-17 shooting while adding five rebounds and two steals. Alperen Sengun contributed 23 points, 10 rebounds and five assists on 9-for-15 shooting.

VanVleet's scoring was secondary on opening night. His ability to organize the offense allowed Durant, Sengun, Smith and Thompson to operate with significantly less responsibility initiating possessions.

Houston will next travel to face the San Antonio Spurs on Friday at 9:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Canadiens lose Nick Suzuki for up to a month due to upper-body injury
articles.summary: The Montreal Canadiens are 4-3-2 on the season, sitting tied for sixth in the Atlantic Division. Still, they have hopes of returning to the playoffs this sea...
articles.body:
The Montreal Canadiens are 4-3-2 on the season, sitting tied for sixth in the Atlantic Division. Still, they have hopes of returning to the playoffs this season after making a run to the conference finals last season. The Habs have already been dealing with plenty of injury concerns this year. The Canadiens have been without Ivan Demidov for much of the season, as he is dealing with a lower-body injury.

Now, the team is dealing with another injury to a star forward , per an announcement from the team.

"Forward Nick Suzuki (upper body) will be out for two to four weeks," the Canadiens announced on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Suzuki was injured when he blocked a shot with his hand late in the game against the San Jose Sharks. He did not speak to the media after the 4-3 overtime loss as he was receiving treatment. The injury will also end his consecutive games played streak , according to Eric Engels of Sportsnet.

"The iron man streak for Suzuki ends at 546 games. Has never missed an NHL game before," Engels posted on X.

Suzuki currently has the second-longest active iron man streak in the NHL at 546 games. He is behind Brent Burns of the Colorado Avalanche, who has played 1017 straight games. Burns could break Phil Kessel's record of consecutive games played this season.

Meanwhile, Suzuki has never missed a game in his NHL career. He was drafted with the 13th overall selection of the 2017 NHL Draft by the Vegas Golden Knights, but was traded to the Canadiens before making his NHL debut. He made his debut with the Canadiens during the 2019-20 season, playing all 71 games that year. Since then, he has played a total of 546 straight games, including 82 games in five straight seasons. In that time, the Canadiens captain has scored 172 goals and added 316 assists. He has five goals and seven assists in nine games this year.

The Canadiens will return to the ice for the first time without Suzuki on Friday night when they visit the Chicago Blackhawks.

articles.title: Flyers rookie Cole Knuble achieves franchise feat not seen in 30 years vs. Sabres
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers have begun to turn their 2026-27 season around, following nine consecutive losses with three straight victories, the latest a 3-1 wi...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Flyers have begun to turn their 2026-27 season around, following nine consecutive losses with three straight victories, the latest a 3-1 win over the Buffalo Sabres at KeyBank Center on Wednesday night.

Rookie Cole Knuble was the hero in Western New York, scoring his first two career goals in just his second NHL game. In the process, he became the first Flyers player in 30 years to record a multi-goal performance within his first two career contests, per NHL.com.

He's the seventh player in franchise history to do so, and the first since Vinny Prospal in 1996-97.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Knuble is the son of longtime NHLer Mike Knuble, who skated in 1,068 career contests, including 338 with the Flyers. He was in attendance to watch his son score twice.

"I've put a lot of work in over the years," Cole Knuble told reporters afterwards, per NHL.com's Heather Engel. "I'm confident in my abilities. It's obviously a jump up, best players in the world. I'm playing with really great teammates, too. Obviously those guys have been great for me."

Knuble opened the scoring late in the first period, collecting a rebound from an Oliver Bonk shot and finishing with a backhand move past Sabres goaltender Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen.

With Philadelphia leading 2-1 early in the third, he banked the puck off Luukkonen's left leg from behind the net to give the Flyers a critical insurance goal.

"I think I can obviously play and help the team at this level, and I think I can bring energy, and I'll do whatever it takes to be a part of this group," Knuble added.

Selected in the fourth round, No. 103 overall, of the 2023 NHL Draft, Knuble spent three seasons with the Notre Dame Fighting Irish.

He produced at close to a point-per-game pace during his tenure in Indiana before finishing the 2025-26 campaign with the American Hockey League's Lehigh Valley Phantoms.

Knuble made an impact during that brief professional stint, recording a goal and two assists in seven games. He began this season with the Phantoms and earned his NHL call-up after posting four points in six contests.

Knuble appears to have earned a longer look in Philadelphia, and he should be in the lineup when the Flyers try to make it four straight wins against the visiting Anaheim Ducks at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Saturday night.

articles.title: Pablo Cardona vuelve a las pistas y avanza en su recuperación: "Estoy viendo la luz al final del túnel"
articles.standfirst: El extremeño, que ha participado en una exhibición en Abu Dhabi de la mano de Hexagon World Series, explica a MARCA cómo va su lesión
articles.summary: El extremeño, que ha participado en una exhibición en Abu Dhabi de la mano de Hexagon World Series, explica a MARCA cómo va su lesión
articles.body: El emeritense Pablo Cardona sorprendía al mundo del pádel a principios de semana compartiendo un post en sus redes sociales en el que ya se le veía dentro del 20x10 pala en mano. Días después ha estado presente en Abu Dhabi disputando una exhibición de la mano de Hexagon World Series, que ha presentado su calendario para 2027. Tras compartir pista con el joven Manu Castaño, el zurdo, que sigue inmerso en el proceso de recuperación de su rodilla y que tuvo que volver a parar tras perderse el tramo final de 2025, volver al lado de Javi Leal y recaer, ha compartido con MARCA sus primeras sensaciones tras volver a vestirse de corto. "Te diría que estoy en uno de los momentos más felices de mi vida. Estoy mejorando muchísimo y creo que estoy viendo la luz al final del túnel", comenzó, con una sonrisa. Sobre la recuperación, fue contundente y claro: aún queda mucho camino por recorrer. "Estoy en ello, voy por el buen camino, pero cada día estoy mejor. Queda trabajar bastante y meterle carga para ponerme fuerte otra vez, que es lo que me falta", añadió. De hecho, durante el Madrid P1 de Premier Padel, hace mes y medio, reconocía a MARCA que estaba en un momento complicado, con ciertas dudas, pero ahora las cosas han cambiado. "Este último mes ha sido brutal en cuanto a mejoría. Luego más adelante contaré todo lo que ha pasado y lo que he tenido que hacer. Estoy cada día un poco mejor, y eso antes no lo veía. Había demasiadas curvas", explica el de Mérida. Precisamente por estar en un evento de Hexagon World Series, la pregunta más repetida hacia el jugador de 22 años era si jugaría esta competición, que arranca el próximo 21 de enero en Madrid. Sobre eso, fue claro: "Bueno, no lo sé. Sobre todo porque dependo de un equipo que me quiera fichar (se ríe). No sé si lo voy a jugar, pero ojalá esté en condiciones de hacerlo". De nuevo, y cuestionado sobre una fecha concreta para volver a la competición, Cardona -que está ahora 252 del ránking FIP- insistió en la cautela y en no repetir los mismos errores que en la primera etapa de la lesión. "No me pongo fecha. Hasta que no esté hecho una bestia, no vuelvo", concluyó.

articles.title: Sri Lanka beat England to overcome Harry Brook hitting fastest 200 in ODIs
articles.summary: England captain Brook hits 202 in record ODI time, but Sri Lanka hit a six to win by two wickets with one ball to spare.
articles.body:
Janith Liyanage smashed a six off the penultimate ball as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, scoring 430-8 to beat England in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

Needing eight to win off the last over, Sri Lanka lost two wickets to paceman Josh Tongue, but Liyanage kept his cool to achieve an astonishing victory and overshadow Harry Brook’s record-setting knock.

The England captain hit the fastest-ever ODI double hundred, making 202 off 116 balls to propel his team to a mammoth 429-4 after they were put in to bat.

South Africa hold the record for the highest ODI chase, knocking off a target of 435 against Australia at Johannesburg in 2006.

Batters thoroughly dominated in Rawalpindi as Brook also hit the first ODI double century by an England player. However, Sri Lanka proved up to the challenge as Pavan Rathnayake scored 130, with Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both making 97.

Liyanage then led them over the line with a blistering 61 not out off 27 balls.

Sri Lanka slid to 24-2 before Rathnayake and Avishka set about transforming the innings, putting on 166 for the third wicket.

Rathnayake then combined with Shanaka to lift the tempo with a rapid 133-run stand off just 79 balls, to give Sri Lanka genuine hope.

Rathnayake hit 15 fours and three sixes while Shanaka’s blazing knock featured eight sixes and six fours, as Sri Lanka delivered a powerful response to Brook’s earlier masterclass.

Brook clobbered 10 sixes and 21 fours as England posted a first 400-plus ODI total in Pakistan.

He reached 200 in 114 balls, beating the previous fastest double century in ODIs by Shubman Gill (117 balls) for India against West Indies last month.

Brook was joined in the fireworks by Joe Root, who scored a 66-ball 69 and became the first England batter to complete 8,000 runs, in his 197th one-day international.

Brook was dismissed off the final delivery, caught off paceman Liyanage, but not before helping England add 156 runs in the last 10 overs.

Opener Tom Banton set the tone with a 51-ball 50, and Will Jacks was 66 not out with three sixes and eight fours.

The day looked as if it would surely belong to history-maker Brook, but Sri Lanka had other ideas as the previous highest ODI total at a Pakistan venue of 375-3 was easily surpassed.

Pakistan, who beat Sri Lanka and England in their two games, will face England in Lahore on Sunday in the next match in the tri-series.

articles.title: Ranking Best NHL Trade Destinations for Dylan Larkin From His Updated 10-Team List
articles.summary: Dylan Larkin's saga may not be at an end, but perhaps his eventual exit from the Detroit Red Wings finally has a roadmap to a resolution.
articles.body:
Dylan Larkin's saga may not be at an end, but perhaps his eventual exit from the Detroit Red Wings finally has a roadmap to a resolution.

Larkin has a list of 10 teams he'd accept a trade to, and given that it all started this summer with three, you could consider this progress…or resignation on Larkin's part, at least. Fortunately for us, a list of 10 teams is pretty ideal to break down and figure out who has the most optimistic chance of acquiring the Detroit centerman who's scored 30 or more goals for five straight seasons.

Of the 10 teams, none of them are located in Canada (sorry, Montréal), and at least two of them have Hughes brothers playing for them. From the East Coast to the Southeast to the Midwest to the Rockies, we'll rank which teams have the best chance to land Dylan Larkin based on NHL players they could part with, prospect pool, picks, and, of course, cap space. Let's get to it.

Any time we do a list of teams that could trade for a star player, Vegas is always included because they'll always do their part to throw their hat in the ring. When it comes to Dylan Larkin, there's no doubt they'd love to do the same for him, but they've got a lot working against them.

Vegas's roster is teeming with players who have trade protection. Whether it's a modified no-trade clause to a full no-move, it's hard to imagine any player who could be part of an offer for Larkin saying yes to going from Las Vegas to Detroit. That's a huge roadblock that also interferes with them being able to free up cap space to make a potential move as well, and since they've got less than $500,000 in cap freedom , that's a problem.

The Golden Knights also lack elite prospects, and while a younger player like Trevor Connelly is proving themselves now, he alone won't be able to land Larkin. Vegas's only hope to pull this off would be a three-team deal to best sort out the no-trade/no-move clauses, but the hoops to jump through might even be too many for them to make it happen.

Just like with Vegas, count out the Florida Panthers from making a big trade at your own peril. But just like the Golden Knights, the Panthers face many of the same obstacles to potentially acquiring Dylan Larkin.

The Panthers have some freedom against the salary cap at the moment thanks to the long-term absences of Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, but with both players expected back before too long, that window to spend against LTIR won't be open long. Florida gets $10 million in relief from Barkov and could have another $5.25 million with Marchand if they put him on LTIR. Jonah Gadjovich's $905,000 is helping them out a little right now as well, according to PuckPedia.com.

The Panthers have been adamant about not trading Anton Lundell, and there's no reason for them to have changed their mind about that, even with someone like Larkin willing to go there. Making this kind of trade within the division isn't unheard of (see Brady Tkachuk, Sam Reinhart), but Lundell would instantly be Detroit's No. 1 center if he were swapped for Larkin, and even though the Panthers are in a better place than the Red Wings, facing up to that for the years to come seems unpleasant even for them.

The Panthers' lack of high-end prospects would also inhibit a trade of this scale, and the eventual need to shift money around could cause other problems. It's not impossible for them to add Larkin, but it would be highly difficult.

The idea of Dylan Larkin joining the Dallas Stars sounds great on paper and fits GM Jim Nill's MO of aiming big to add to the team, but the Stars might have a better chance to acquire him after this season than during it.

While the Stars have to get Jason Robertson extended before he hits free agency, they're also set to watch Tyler Seguin's $9.85 million contract end, as well as $1.5 million from Tyler Myers, after this season. Ideally, Robertson's next contract commands a big chunk of that up from his current $12 million hit, but likely not by so much that it would impede adding Larkin's $8.7 million.

If Dallas could make a trade happen this season to add Larkin, they'd be putting themselves in the driver's seat to be Cup contenders for even longer. But how they can put together a trade package to appease the Red Wings is tricky, given they've got their top guys locked up long-term and most of them with trade protection (aside from Wyatt Johnston, curiously). Prospects like Emil Hemming, Cameron Schmidt, and 2026 second-round pick defenseman Jakub Vaněček would almost certainly have to be included, but the Stars' pool of elite prospects is already thin enough.

Quick Predictions on Biggest Storylines 💭

If you told Red Wings fans 20 years ago that one day they could trade their now-former captain and top forward to the Colorado Avalanche, you'd probably be told you're out of your mind.

Times change, and so do needs and rivalries.

Dylan Larkin saying he'd be happy going to Denver still likely rankles more than a few fans in Detroit. But if there's an upside to this for those disgruntled Wings fans, the Avalanche haven't got a great case to make for the former captain. While Colorado adding Larkin would be more than a coup in the Western Conference, what they could offer Detroit for him might not be enough to keep Shawn Horcoff on the phone.

Veterans like Nicolas Roy, Fedor Svechkov, Parker Kelly and Noah Juulsen don't have trade protection, and while their combined cap hits could make way for Larkin, it's hard to see Detroit being motivated by them. Perhaps adding Scott Wedgewood would help, but prospects would be necessary from Colorado to sweeten that pot, and they're running thin on top ones after being Stanley Cup contenders for the past few years.

If Dylan Larkin wanting a trade out of Detroit wasn't hard enough to stomach for the Red Wings and their fans, his desire to go to division rivals is enough to see red. But for interim GM Shawn Horcoff, the Tampa Bay Lightning offer curious potential.

If the Lightning wanted to make a run at Larkin, freeing up money to make it happen would be tricky but not impossible. They've got a few million in cap space already, and they have a handful of roster players they could send to Detroit to help them bring on Larkin and his $8.7 million cap hit.

Although those potential players won't totally move the needle for Detroit, adding a prospect like Ethan Czata or younger players like Conor Geekie and Dominic James could help bring them to the table. Then again, the Lightning haven't been perpetually successful by emptying out their coffers of young players, particularly to division rivals.

What could make pursuing Larkin most intimidating? Nikita Kucherov's impending big-time extension: they'd like to get him signed to before he becomes a free agent this summer. A luxury addition like Larkin would assuredly make getting that done far more difficult, given that Larkin's contract has four more years beyond this one remaining.

Of the teams in the race for Dylan Larkin, the Wild have been, reportedly, the most aggressive. Rumors of an offer turned down have swirled, and with GM Bill Guerin known for being active in the market at all times, it would make sense.

The Wild can offer roster players to make the money work, and the handful of top prospects in the organization are interesting, but any of their best players are already helping the Wild out in the NHL. If Detroit had interest in a goalie, Jesper Wallstedt or (currently injured) Filip Gustavsson would be more than good enough to get talks going, but the Wings have John Gibson and are high on their own prospect, Trey Augustine.

Minnesota, meanwhile, is most busy trying to get Quinn Hughes signed to an extension and there's a theory that landing Larkin could help them retain Hughes thanks to their shared glory with Team USA at the Olympics. That might be a mild stretch, but if Minnesota finding a way to land Larkin was what it took to retain Hughes long-term, Guerin would have to make that happen no matter what, wouldn't he? Picks and prospects might not be enough to get Detroit to say yes, especially since those picks likely won't be high first-rounders.

Dylan Larkin joining the Washington Capitals sounds like the kind of move that would be impossible, but one look at the Caps' salary structure, roster, and how things look down the road says otherwise.

What the Capitals lack in salary room now to add Larkin could be made up quickly if they were willing to move Dylan Strome in such an offer. Strome's $5 million cap hit would cover more than half of Larkin's $8.7 million hit, for example. Washington has enough movable contracts and potentially maneuverable no-trade clauses to even out the money.

The Capitals have enough NHL-experienced players to make a deal happen, and if Detroit wanted prospects, that could be a bit stickier but not a total deal-breaker. But if Detroit's insistence is on making a "hockey trade" for Larkin, the Capitals might provide them with one of the better opportunities.

New Devils GM Sunny Mehta is a guy we're still getting to know when it comes to making deals, so the possibility of New Jersey making a run at Dylan Larkin is loaded with mystery.

What we know about the Devils is that they've got players who could make a deal happen. Forwards Dawson Mercer and Arseny Gritsyuk would be attractive to the Red Wings, as would prospect defensemen Anton Silaev and Seamus Casey. Moving guys like Mercer and/or Gritsyuk would help free up cap space, and including a top prospect like Silaev would certainly appeal to Detroit. The question here is whether it would be enough to make the Red Wings happy.

Oddly enough, like the Wild, the Devils have the future to consider, which could involve Quinn Hughes joining his brothers Jack and Luke in Newark. If Hughes doesn't sign long-term with the Wild, keeping future salary cap space free to sign Quinn Hughes would be wise for New Jersey. But teams want to win now, and if landing Larkin helps the Devils right away, making that move and figuring out how to land Quinn in the offseason can be a tomorrow problem.

The Devils can make an interesting offer for Larkin and at least get Detroit on the phone with players, prospects, and picks, but the prospect of reuniting the Hughes clan looms.

The Hurricanes didn't get to be Stanley Cup champions last season without being aggressive, and with Dylan Larkin out there and saying he'd happily go to Carolina, exploring that move makes a lot of sense.

Larkin would give the Hurricanes another top offensive weapon and yet another player for them to stifle opponents by driving shots to the net and maintaining offensive zone possession. What's more, Carolina has Alexander Nikishin to dangle in an offer, although given the Red Wings' difficulty in getting their own RFA defenseman Simon Edvinsson re-signed, attempting to do the same with Nikishin seems foreboding, given he could just as well go back to Russia to play if he were unhappy with the trade.

Still, Carolina has more than Nikishin to use in a trade if they wanted to push for Larkin. They've already got plenty of cap space, so moving money to add Larkin isn't an issue. They have prospects like Bradly Nadeau, Felix Unger Sörum, Charlie Cerrato and Joel Nystrom to entice Detroit (among others), not to mention a veteran like Jesperi Kotkaniemi if the Wings required NHL talent in return.

A reason for Detroit to be wary of Carolina in making a trade? Hurricanes GM Eric Tulsky generally gets his way against even the most experienced GMs.

In Larkin's revised list of teams he's willing to accept a trade to, Utah was arguably the most surprising one. The Mammoth aren't in the same tier as Stanley Cup contenders like Carolina, Colorado, Vegas, or Dallas, but they're young and on the rise and already made the playoffs last season. They're also a team that could make a spectacular offer to the Red Wings.

Utah's young core of Clayton Keller, Larkin's Olympic teammate Logan Cooley, and Dylan Guenther is a reason to want to join the Mammoth alone. With Mikhail Sergachev and MacKenzie Weegar leading the way on defense and Karel Vejmelka holding it down in net, the Mammoth are fun.

To be able to add Larkin, they've got up-and-coming young players like Dmitri Simashev, Daniil But, Caleb Desnoyers, Tij Iginla, Maveric Lamoureux, Max Psenicka and Michal Hrabal either in Utah or on the way in a year or two; that's a lot of ammo for a trade. Even though Utah is reportedly also in the mix for Connor Hellebuyck, they've got enough going on prospect-wise to add both if they wanted to get hyper aggressive. But for Larkin, they've got plenty of assets to use to not just get Detroit on the phone but to close the deal as well.

articles.title: Cristian Zapata, la última locura del Real Montevideo: el club de la cuarta uruguaya que se maneja por una app
articles.standfirst: El equipo lanzó un juego, Real Manager, por el que los hinchas deciden que fichajes hace el club
articles.summary: El equipo lanzó un juego, Real Manager, por el que los hinchas deciden que fichajes hace el club
articles.body: El fútbol sudamericano siempre tiene la capacidad de reinventarse y sorprendernos con historias inverosímiles, pero lo que está gestando el Real Montevideo supera cualquier guion de película. Este humilde club, que compite en la Primera D (la cuarta y última categoría del fútbol uruguayo), decidió patear el tablero y armar un plantel con nombres estelares de jerarquía internacional, combinando nostalgia, marketing y una ambición desmedida. La gran bomba que encendió la ilusión de los hinchas es la incorporación del experimentado defensor colombiano Cristian Zapata. A sus 40 años, el mundialista con la Selección Colombia y de pasado ilustre en clubes como el Milan de Italia, saldrá de su retiro para ponerse la camiseta del conjunto uruguayo. Su llegada no solo aporta veteranía y jerarquía defensiva a un equipo de la 'D', sino que posiciona inmediatamente al club en el foco mediático continental. “Cristian Zapata está confirmado. Nos puede dar solidez defensiva. La idea es tenerlo para todos los playoffs y, si no se puede, que juegue aunque sea un partido”, declaró el presidente del club, Pedro del Campo a Sport 890. Lejos de conformarse con el zaguero colombiano —y con la reciente incorporación del delantero panameño Kahiser Lenis (con paso por la última Copa América y Atlético Goianiense)—, la directiva del Real Montevideo va por más. Los directivos confirmaron públicamente que se encuentran en avanzadas negociaciones con pesos pesados retirados o en el tramado final de sus carreras. Entre los apuntados figuran el mítico argentino Ariel 'Burrito' Ortega y Mariano 'Tanque' Pavone. “Estamos en tratativas por el Tanque Pavone y el Burrito Ortega. Nuestro sueño es que vuelva a jugar al fútbol profesionalmente contra Boca Juniors de Uruguay, que es en dos fechas. Estamos ahí. Si se da, se da”, deslizaron desde la cúpula dirigencial, evidenciando que el timing y la repercusión de los partidos son parte central de esta estrategia. Asimismo, el nombre de un guerrero temperamental como el brasileño Felipe Melo también aparece en el radar de deseos de la institución. El proyecto de Real Montevideo no apunta únicamente a lo deportivo dentro del verde césped, sino a transformar cada fin de semana en un evento cultural y de atracción masiva. La directiva ha creado un modelo por el que los hinchas pueden manejar el club por medio una app, Real Manager: “Si la gente se copa, la idea es que los hinchas elijan qué figuras vamos a buscar”, señalaron sobre la hoja de ruta a futuro. La iniciativa tuvo la intervención del influencer El Scarso, quien se hizo reconocido durante el Mundial por hacer famoso al jugador neozelandés Tim Payne. La idea a la que contribuido consiste en un juego por el que los simpatizantes pueden tomar las decisiones del club en todos sus ámbitos, hasta decidir sus fichajes. Mientras tanto, el mundo del ascenso uruguayo asiste perplejo a esta revolución insólita. Pasar de las canchas modestas del conurbano montevideano a soñar con leyendas de la talla de Zapata, Ortega, Pavone o Melo demuestra que, en el fútbol, la ilusión no entiende de categorías. Real Montevideo ya consiguió lo más difícil: que todo el continente hable de ellos.

articles.title: Bayern Múnich confirma lesión de Luis Díaz y se perdería la próxima fecha de la Selección Colombia
articles.standfirst: El delantero colombiano sufre un desgarro muscular leve en el partido contra el Arsenal
articles.summary: El delantero colombiano sufre un desgarro muscular leve en el partido contra el Arsenal
articles.body: El Bayern Múnich confirmó el diagnóstico médico de Luis Díaz tras el partido frente al Arsenal por la UEFA Champions League, encuentro en el cual el extremo colombiano tuvo que abandonar el terreno de juego anticipadamente. Las noticias hacen ver que el extremo podría estar varias semanas por fuera y perderse también la próxima convocatoria de la Selección Colombia en los amistosos de noviembre. De acuerdo con el comunicado emitido por el club alemán, el atacante sufre una pequeña rotura fibrilar (desgarro leve) en la parte posterior del muslo izquierdo. La dolencia se originó en los minutos finales del compromiso europeo, encendiendo de inmediato las alarmas en el cuerpo técnico comandado por Vincent Kompany y en la Selección Colombia. “Luis Díaz sufrió una pequeña rotura fibrilar en la parte posterior del muslo izquierdo durante el partido de la Liga de Campeones que enfrentó al FC Bayern contra el Arsenal. Así lo han revelado los exámenes realizados por el departamento médico del conjunto bávaro. El delantero de 29 años será, por lo tanto, baja por el momento”, dice el comunicado. Aunque el conjunto bávaro indicó inicialmente que el jugador estará de baja "por el momento" y su evolución se evaluará partido a partido, los pronósticos médicos para este tipo de lesiones estipulan un periodo de recuperación estimado entre dos y cuatro semanas. Esta baja representa un duro golpe para el Gigante de Baviera en un tramo exigente del calendario, ya que el guajiro se perdería compromisos cruciales tanto a nivel doméstico —incluyendo partidos de la Bundesliga y la Copa de Alemania— como europeos, el duelo del próximo 3 de noviembre frente al Atlético. Del mismo modo, su presencia queda en entredicho para la próxima doble fecha de amistosos con la Selección Colombia en el mes de noviembre, a la espera de ver cómo evoluciona favorablemente bajo la supervisión del departamento médico alemán.
