articles.title: Luis Díaz y Luis Suárez, los únicos colombianos en los 100 de MARCA
articles.standfirst: Los delanteros referentes del Bayern y el Sporting se colocan en el prestigioso listado
articles.summary: Los delanteros referentes del Bayern y el Sporting se colocan en el prestigioso listado
articles.body: Luis Díaz y Luis Suárez se han convertido en los únicos dos colombianos en aparecer en la lista de los 100 de MARCA. Los dos delanteros de la Tricolor han recibido el premio a su gran temporada en la que se han erigido como auténticos referentes de sus equipos. El delantero samario Luis Javier Suárez, referente del Sporting de Portugal, se posiciona en el lugar 85 del ranking de los 100 de MARCA. Suárez ha demostrado una regularidad imponentemente alta, registrando 31 contribuciones de gol (entre anotaciones y asistencias) en 34 partidos disputados durante este 2026. Su impresionante efectividad de cara al arco lo ha puesto incluso por encima de nombres estelares del fútbol europeo como Undav o Semenyo, consolidándose como la gran carta de gol en su club y ratificando el porqué de su cotización en la élite internacional. Por su parte, Luis Díaz, extremo estrella del Bayern Múnich, ocupa la casilla 26 del prestigioso listado de los 100 de MARCA. Aunque 'Lucho' ha tenido un arranque de temporada un tanto más dosificado en materia de redes contrarias con el gigante alemán, el acumulado colosal que cosechó a lo largo de todo el año lo sostiene firmemente en el Top mundial con 30 contribuciones en 36 encuentros. El extremo guajiro se mantiene así como uno de los atacantes más desequilibrantes y respetados del panorama europeo, superando a pesos pesados y confirmando que su impacto colectivo sigue intacto. Muestra de ello es su posición entre los 30 mejores de este listado.

articles.title: Hashimoto extiende su reinado con un cuarto oro consecutivo en el concurso completo
articles.standfirst: El japonés supera con autoridad al chino Haonan Yang y el británico Joe Fraser en una final que remató en la barra fija
articles.summary: El japonés supera con autoridad al chino Yang Haonan y el británico Joe Fraser en una final que remató en la barra fija
articles.body: Daiki Hashimoto está cada vez más cerca de su ídolo Kōhei Uchimura y sus seis títulos mundiales consecutivos (entre 2009 y 2015) en el concurso completo. De momento suma cuatro, tras imponerse este jueves en la final del campeonato que se disputa en Rotterdam (Países Bajos). El gimnasta japonés, de 25 años y conocido por su estricta disciplina a la hora de entrenar, sumó 85,998 puntos y aventajó en 1,799 al chino Haonan Yang, plata con 84,199, y en casi dos y medio al británico Joe Fraser, que completó el podio con una puntuación de 83,531. Hashimoto tuvo que esperar a su último ejercicio en la barra fija para rematar su triunfo pero ya había sido el mejor de los 24 finalistas en el caballo con arcos y las barras paralelas. Sólo desentonó nada más comenzar en el suelo -décima nota- pero sumados los seis aparatos volvió a no tener rival. Gimnasta desde los seis años por influencia de sus hermanos mayores, ya había hecho historia en los Juegos de Tokio de 2020 al convertirse en el campeón olímpico del concurso completo masculino más joven de la historia con apenas 19 años y 355 días. Una caída en el caballo con arco en París 2024 evitó que revalidara su título olímpico -acabó sexto- pero desde entonces tiene entre ceja y ceja el oro en Los Ángeles 2028 para igualar los dos títulos olímpicos en el concurso completo de Uchimura. Por su parte, el joven colombiano Ángel Barajas, medallista de plata en barra fija en los Juegos Olímpicos de París, dio un nuevo paso hacia adelante en su meteórica carrera y concluyó quinto, un puesto por encima de la sexta plaza que logró el pasado año en Yakarta, con una nota final de 83,232 puntos.

articles.title: World Artistic Gymnastics Championships: Joe Fraser wins all-around bronze as Jake Jarman comes sixth
articles.summary: Great Britain's Joe Fraser wins bronze in the all-around final at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam.
articles.body:
Great Britain's Joe Fraser bounced back from the disappointment of Wednesday's team final to win all-around bronze at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam.

The 27-year-old finished with a score of 83.531 after the six disciplines to become just the third British man to win a world all-around medal, after Dan Keatings and Max Whitlock won silver in 2009 and 2014 respectively.

Japan's Daiki Hashimoto scored 85.988 to win his fourth successive all-around gold at a World Championships, while China's Haonan Yang took silver with 84.199.

Britain's Jake Jarman narrowly missed out on the podium with a score of 82.865, but his sixth-place finish means it is the best result by a pair of British men in the all-around event at a World Championships.

Fraser celebrated his bronze medal with a thumb-sucking gesture - a nod to his pregnant girlfriend who was watching from home.

"I've got a pregnant girlfriend at home with four weeks to go, we've had a team final to qualify for the Olympic Games and sadly didn't make it and I've gone out there today and managed to pick up a bronze medal," Fraser told BBC Sport.

"It's been a real whirlwind but I have loved every second and I'm grateful to be out there in amongst the best in the world.

"We had a lot of fun out there. It's just the icing on the cake to bring this home."

Britain finished fourth in the men's team event on Wednesday which meant they failed to book their place at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles, although they will get another chance to qualify at next year's World Championships.

Jarman, who will compete in the floor final on Saturday, believes the British team "have a lot to give" before LA 2028.

"The potential that we've got looking to LA, it's promising, it's exciting," he told BBC Sport.

"I think we have got a lot to give and I can't wait to see where we are in two years' time."

articles.title: Midweek availability report for Michigan State versus No. 9 UCLA
articles.summary: Michigan State has announced that 11 players are ruled out with injuries for Week 8 against UCLA in the Rose Bowl.
articles.body:
The Week 8 availability reports for Saturday's UCLA Bruins - Michigan State Spartans showdown were made available and the Bruins appear to be heading into the game with a better health situation than the 2-5 Spartans .

Michigan State has already ruled 11 players out for Saturday's game at the Rose Bowl, with another six players listed as questionable. UCLA isn't in a great spot injury-wise either, with Nico Iamaleava set to miss the rest of the season after undergoing surgery .

UCLA has ruled out seven players themselves, with the list including Iamaleava, wide receivers Mikey Matthews and Jonah Smith, offensive linemen Jordan Davis and Sam Yoon, defensive backs Tao Johnson and Rodrick Pleasant. The Bruins also have offensive lineman Eugene Brooks listed as probable.

It's been impressive how UCLA's depth has made the most of their opportunities this season under Bob Chesney. The Bruins have used offensive line rotations throughout the season, have seen backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach step up in a moment's notice and new names step up and make big plays at wide receiver and in their secondary.

UCLA's depth is why they're 6-0 and are the No. 9 team in the country entering Saturday's game. We'll see how the Spartans handle potentially missing over a dozen players this week. Michigan State will enter the game having lost five games in a row.

Michigan State is still searching for their first Big Ten win this season, already having lost to Nebraska, Wisconsin, Illinois and Northwestern. The lone common opponent is Wisconsin, who UCLA defeated 17-7 while the Spartans fell 31-3 on the road in Madison.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli ready to "finish the job" as first F1 title chance beckons at US GP
articles.summary: At this weekend's Formula 1 United States Grand Prix, Kimi Antonelli gets a first, if unlikely, match point to clinch his maiden world championship
articles.body:
Formula 1's runaway leader Kimi Antonelli says he will try to "finish the job properly" as he gets a first opportunity to become the series' youngest ever world champion.

The 20-year-old can clinch the 2026 title as early as this weekend's United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas, though this scenario would involve getting some outside help.

Antonelli will win the title if he wins Sunday's race and Mercedes team-mate George Russell - who is 102 points behind - finishes ninth or lower, and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finishes no higher than fifth.

When asked about that possibility, Antonelli vowed he would try to "finish the job properly", which means approaching the Austin-Mexico-Brazil triple-header as he would any other race.

This is the same approach that has netted him the eight grand prix wins and 14 podiums that have got the Italian to this point.

"It definitely is crazy if you think about it, but that's why I won't think about it," Antonelli said. "Something catastrophic to others needs to happen and for me it needs to be a perfect weekend, which is unlikely to happen.

"We had a meeting with Bono [race engineer Peter Bonnington] this morning and we said to just have fun and always have the same mindset as I had all year.

"One race at a time and just try to do the best I can every race weekend and then we'll see. But of course, if I do things well, then the result will come."

Antonelli admitted a title success would be the fulfilment of a childhood dream and an "incredible achievement", but vowed to "finish the job properly" first.

"It would be a dream, it's something I've dreamt of since I was little. First of all to find myself in such a position is incredible," he added.

"But at the same time, I need to keep going, keep pushing and it's not over yet. First we'll try to finish the job properly and then we can enjoy the rest. But for sure, it will be an incredible achievement."

articles.title: NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series Preview: Jesse Love Looks to Extend Championship Lead at Talladega
articles.summary: The NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series heads to Talladega Superspeedway on Saturday for The Progress Group 250, a crucial race as the championship Chase enter...
articles.body:
The NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series heads to Talladega Superspeedway on Saturday for The Progress Group 250, a crucial race as the championship Chase enters its final stretch. With only three races remaining in the Chase, the pressure is increasing for drivers fighting to secure the championship, and Talladega's unpredictable racing could dramatically change the standings.

The 94-lap race is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on The CW, with 41 cars entered for the event.

Jesse Love enters the weekend leading the championship standings after winning at Phoenix Raceway. The Richard Childress Racing driver holds a 36-point advantage over Justin Allgaier, putting himself in a strong position as the series heads to one of its most unpredictable tracks.

Love has been impressive throughout the Chase, combining race-winning speed with consistency. He also has a strong history at Talladega, recording finishes of 10th or better in five career starts at the track, including a victory in 2024.

However, superspeedway racing presents unique challenges. Drivers must work together in drafting packs, make smart decisions in traffic and avoid the accidents that can end a race in an instant. Love will need to balance racing aggressively for stage points with protecting his championship lead.

Allgaier and the Challengers Need a Big Day

Justin Allgaier enters Talladega second in the standings and needs a strong result to close the gap. The JR Motorsports veteran has the experience to navigate the closing laps, but he will need to capitalize on every opportunity to gain points.

Sheldon Creed is another driver to watch. Despite an engine problem at Phoenix that resulted in a 32nd place finish, Creed has been one of the series' most consistent performers this season. He has also shown strong speed at Talladega, finishing third earlier this year after battling for the win on the final lap.

Sam Mayer and Austin Hill could also play important roles. Hill is the defending fall winner at Talladega, while Mayer has demonstrated the ability to compete near the front on superspeedways.

The 2.66-mile track is famous for close racing, massive drafting packs and dramatic finishes. Stage breaks are scheduled for laps 25 and 50, giving drivers additional opportunities to collect valuable points.

For Love, the goal is to leave Alabama with his championship lead intact. For his challengers, the mission is to take advantage of one of the final opportunities to make a major move.

With the Chase approaching its conclusion, Saturday's race could prove pivotal in determining who enters the final two races with the strongest championship position.

articles.title: Ron Duguay, charismatic New York Rangers star who finished NHL career with Kings, dies at 69
articles.summary: Ron Duguay, a longtime New York Rangers star who finished his NHL career with the Kings, has died of cancer.
articles.body:
Ron Duguay , a longtime New York Rangers star who finished his NHL career with the Kings , has died of cancer. He was 69.

The Rangers announced the loss of "one of the most popular players in franchise history" on Thursday morning after being informed by Duguay's family.

"Ron's signature skating style — with his hair flowing as he moved down the ice — captivated The Garden Faithful, and his skill, tenacity, and charisma earned him the admiration of all New Yorkers," the team said in a statement. "We join the hockey community in sending our condolences to Ron's friends, family, and loved ones during this difficult time."

Former Alaska governor and 2008 Republican U.S. vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin , who dated Duguay over the last several years, posted on social media that the one-time NHL All-Star "passed away peacefully" Thursday "after a hard-fought battle with cancer."

"It's with a shattered heart, but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now," Palin wrote . "He fought so hard. Love never ends."

On Sunday, Palin posted photos that appeared to show her holding Duguay's hand while he was in a hospital bed. "Prayers for Ron Duguay are felt & appreciated," she wrote .

Born in Sudbury, Ontario, Duguay was selected by the Rangers at No. 13 overall in the 1977 draft. Known for his long, curly hair and flashy lifestyle — "why, he even danced with Cher at one of Manhattan's best-known discos," the New York Times wrote in 1983 — Duguay became a star during the six seasons of his initial stint in New York. He helped the Rangers make the 1979 Stanley Cup Final and earned his only All-Star nod in 1982.

Duguay was traded to the Detroit Red Wings in the summer of 1983 and had the two best seasons of his career, including career highs of 89 points on 38 goals and 51 assists during the 1984-1985 season. He also played for the Pittsburgh Penguins and a second time for the Rangers before wrapping up his career with the Kings from 1988 to 1989.

Overall, Duguay had 673 points (305 goals, 368 assists) in the NHL regular season and playoffs. He went on to play in the minor leagues, including two seasons with the IHL's San Diego Gulls , and spent 12 years calling Rangers games as an MSG Network analyst.

"Ron greeted each day with the biggest smile, an incredible zest for life, and a positive outlook that shone through everything he saw, everything he did, and every life he touched," the NHL Alumni Assn. wrote on X . "He will be remembered not only for the player he was, but for the extraordinary person he was. His warmth, his laughter, his kindness, and his beautiful spirit will forever remain in the hearts of his family, friends, teammates, and the entire NHL Alumni community."

The Kings reposted the alumni association's statement and added : "Our hearts are with Ron's family & loved ones and we join them in mourning his passing."

In 2024, Duguay was diagnosed with Stage 4 cancer, which had started in his colon before spreading to his liver and other parts of his body, according to a post on the GoFundMe page set up by his three adult children to help pay for his medical and travel costs. He lived in Florida but had to make regular trips to Orange County for treatment.

"Early this morning, our beloved father took his final breath after fighting a long and courageous battle. He fought with everything he had, right until the very end," daughter Shay Thomas wrote on Thursday in a separate GoFundMe post. "Our hearts are shattered, and the world feels a little less bright without him in it. He will be missed by so many, but we find peace in knowing that he is finally free from pain and suffering.

"He fought the good fight until his very last breath, and today, Heaven gained a truly special angel."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Rangers Given Clear Warning Over Celtic Title Race: Can McInnes Exploit Their European Advantage?
articles.summary: Rangers have little room for another domestic slip-up if they want to close the gap on Celtic in the Scottish Premiership. With no European fixtures to manag...
articles.body:
Rangers have little room for another domestic slip-up if they want to close the gap on Celtic in the Scottish Premiership. With no European fixtures to manage, Derek McInnes' side have a clear advantage in their pursuit of the league leaders, but recent results suggest they still need greater consistency.

The Ibrox side missed a valuable opportunity last weekend. Rangers surrendered a lead to draw 2-2 against Dundee on October 17, allowing Celtic to strengthen their position with a crushing 7-1 victory over Hearts the following day. That result left the Light Blues four points behind their city rivals, increasing the pressure ahead of Saturday's home match against St Johnstone.

According to comments reported in the Scottish football discussion on The Breakdown podcast, relayed by BBC , former Rangers midfielder Kevin Thomson believes the fixture schedule should favour McInnes' team over the coming weeks.

Rangers have no continental matches after their European qualifying campaign ended in defeat on penalties against Jablonec. Celtic, meanwhile, have at least six more Europa League fixtures to negotiate, beginning with Thursday's home meeting with Celta Vigo.

Thomson argued that playing before Celtic allows Rangers to put their rivals under pressure. A victory against St Johnstone could cut the deficit to one point before Martin O'Neill's side visit Hibernian on Sunday.

The former midfielder also suggested that Rangers could supply more players than Celtic in a combined Old Firm starting XI, reflecting his confidence in the squad's individual quality.

"The bit I think that favours Rangers, or it should, and there can't be any excuses from a blue perspective, is they've not got Europe," former Rangers midfielder Thomson said on The Breakdown podcast.

"The likelihood is they're going to play in front of Celtic week after week. It'll not happen every week, obviously. But it's that psychological aspect of being able to win on the Saturday.

"It's St Johnstone at Ibrox on Saturday and if Celtic were to potentially have a hard European game (against Vigo) and then they have to go to Easter Road on Sunday. They could still go to Easter Road and win, but I think that's the exciting part about this title race."

Thomson, in a discussion with former Celtic player Charlie Mulgrew about a combined current Old Firm XI, added: "I still think you would pick more Rangers players (than Celtic) in a starting 11 now."

Can Rangers turn their scheduling advantage into a title-winning run?

GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – SEPTEMBER 13: Rangers manager Derek McInnes celebrates at full time after a 3-0 victory during the Rangers v Celtic – Premier Sports Cup match at Ibrox Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

McInnes must make that advantage count on the pitch. Rangers have collected 20 points from nine league matches, recording six wins, two draws and one defeat while scoring 13 goals and conceding seven. Five victories in their previous six league games had strengthened their position before the frustrating draw at Dundee interrupted their progress.

The defensive record offers encouragement, but Rangers need an efficient attacking threat when opponents defend deep. Their European absence gives the squad more recovery time, yet fatigue alone won't determine the title race.

Celtic can still win domestic matches after demanding European nights, as their demolition of Hearts demonstrated. Rangers, therefore, need to concentrate on their own performances rather than wait for their rivals to stumble.

Saturday's match is important. Dropping points against St Johnstone would waste another opportunity to narrow the gap and hand Celtic greater freedom on Sunday. McInnes must demand a convincing performance, clinical finishing and concentration until the final whistle.

Thomson's argument makes sense, but the psychological advantage works both ways. Winning first can unsettle Celtic; failing to do so can expose Rangers to greater scrutiny. With 20 points already secured, the Ibrox side remain firmly involved in the contest, although their next domestic performance must justify the confidence surrounding their title ambitions.

articles.title: Top ranked Texas program gets star QB back, but not its three vacated wins
articles.summary: After missing four games due to an ineligibility ruling, one of the state's best QBs returns to the ranked team.
articles.body:
One of Texas's best high school quarterbacks has come full circle.

On Thursday, the University Interscholastic League (UIL) state executive committee reversed its eligibility ruling on Lewisville junior quarterback Laykon Brassfield . The Fighting Farmers star is now eligible to return to the field after missing four games, but their three vacated wins will not be reinstated.

Brassfield's appeal passed by a unanimous vote after the DEC initially voted 7-0 to rule him ineligible after he transferred from Edmond North in Oklahoma to the North Texas school after his sophomore year. The DEC's initial investigation found that Brassfield did not actually reside in Lewisville and declared he could not participate in varsity competition for one calendar year from the date he enrolled at Lewisville.

According to UIL executive director Jamey Harrison, the earlier ruling was a "reasonable" at the time

Initial residency questions arose regarding an apartment in Lewisville and a house in Argyle owned by Laykon's grandfather, which was used to enroll his younger siblings in Argyle ISD. Brassfield's father, Jonathan, stated this was to meet the children's educational needs. Attorney Brian Wcislo said the situation was previously disclosed on Lewisville ISD and AISD Athletic Participation Forms.

Jonathan Brassfield, Laykon's father, confirmed he was a financial guarantor for the Argyle house while the family lived in a 600-square-foot apartment in Lewisville. They have since moved to a 1,200-square-foot apartment in the Lewisville attendance zone, removed the guarantor status from the Argyle residency, and transferred Laykon's siblings out of Argyle.

"I want to reinforce, as a family, we have lived in Lewisville. This has been our home," Jonathan said Thursday. "I certainly hate that there has been confusion in the paperwork that has interrupted my son's life. I take full responsibility for some confusion on the paperwork, but we live in Lewisville; we've lived in Lewisville. We love it here."

Lewisville remains "undefeated" without Brassfield

Brassfield, named a team captain in his first year with the program, led the Farmers to a 3-0 start and looked like one of the state's best quarterbacks. The Fighting Farmers quarterback threw for 734 passing yards, 14 passing touchdowns and just one interception. On the ground, he added 133 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.

Without their star quarterback, Lewisville has continued to win big, remaining undefeated in district play and outscoring their last four opponents 157-25. Lewisville backup quarterback Aiden Evans, who also stars at defensive back and is committed to Sam Houston State, has thrown for 393 yards and run for 359 yards, with eight total touchdowns-four passing, four rushing.

Brassfield will officially return to action as the No. 11-ranked Fighting Farmers look to lock up a district title against rival Flower Mound on Friday night. It's not immediately clear whether Evans or Brassfield will start at quarterback, but both will likely see the field in the pivotal matchup.

articles.title: Colorado vs. Oklahoma State score predictions, game picks for Week 8
articles.summary: Colorado travels to a hostile Boone Pickens Stadium to take on an explosive Oklahoma State team. Our staff predicts Saturday's matchup.
articles.body:
The Colorado Buffaloes have another chance to snap their losing streak Saturday, but it won't be easy as they face one of college football's best offenses: the Oklahoma State Cowboys .

Colorado enter the matchup with four straight losses, but showed signs of an offensive breakout in a 27-24 loss to No. 11 Utah. Still, it wasn't a perfect performance, and penalties and a costly late turnover proved too much to overcome. Were the signs for what's to come, or will the Buffs fall back into a lull against a talented Oklahoma State team?

The Cowboys boast arguably the Big 12's top quarterback in Drew Mestemaker, who has generated Heisman Trophy buzz . He leads an offense that averages over 500 yards per game and nearly 330 passing yards. OSU"s defense has struggled at times, potentially giving Isaac Wilson and Colorado's offense an opportunity to build on last week.

Here's how the Buffaloes Wire staff predicts Saturday's Big 12 showdown between Colorado and Oklahoma State will unfold.

If Colorado had a better offense, I believe they would win this game. However, the Buffaloes haven't been able to play consistently on offense all season, while Oklahoma State has consistently put points on the board. Their quarterback, Drew Mestemaker, is considered a long shot for the Heisman. But being in the Heisman conversation says a lot about how good he is. Colorado's defense will keep them in this game for a while, as it did against Texas Tech and Utah, but the offense will be the reason the Buffaloes leave with a loss.

I'm taking Oklahoma State because I don't trust Colorado to score points right now. Drew Mestemaker is the biggest reason I'm picking the Cowboys. Colorado will need consistent pressure from Lamont Lester and Santana Hopper to keep him from settling into the passing game. The Buffaloes showed progress in their 27-24 loss to Utah, and I expect JaQuail Smith to stay involved, but Oklahoma State can score points, and I expect them to pull away at home.

Colorado has lost eight straight Big 12 games. Let that sink in for a minute. Still, the Buffaloes kept the game close against Utah, and Isaac Wilson once again sparked the offense despite a back-breaking late-game turnover. To win, the Buffs need to force turnovers from Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker and give their offense a short field to exploit a leaky Cowboys defense.

I am more confident in the Buffaloes' offense after last week, but I still see some big question marks, and I think the defense cracks a bit against the high-flying Cowboys, and one big mistake, whether a penalty or turnover, bites the Buffs late.

articles.title: Robert Garcia tips Albert Gonzalez to replicate world title success of Bam Rodriguez
articles.summary: The featherweight division has plenty of talent, led by titleholders Rafael Espinoza (WBO), Angelo Leo (IBF), and Bruce Carrington (WBC). Brandon Figueroa wa...
articles.body:
The featherweight division has plenty of talent, led by titleholders Rafael Espinoza (WBO), Angelo Leo (IBF), and Bruce Carrington (WBC). Brandon Figueroa was the WBA champion, but he recently failed to make weight for his first defence and was stripped. None of the champions is overly active, and no unification fights seem likely anytime soon. Hot on the heels of the champions is the unbeaten Albert Gonzalez. "Chop Chop" is guided by renowned trainer Robert Garcia, who recently spoke to The Ring , tipping Gonzalez to replicate the success of Jesse "Bam" Rodriguez.

Albert Gonzalez set to shine on Navarrete vs Foster undercard

On October 24, "Chop Chop" Gonzalez (18-0, 11 KOs) will return to action against Edward Vazquez (20-3, 6 KOs). Vazquez has won three consecutive fights since being stopped against Espinoza.

Gonzalez has won his last four by stoppage and seems to be improving with every fight. Under the tutelage of Robert Garcia, it's easy to see why many feel "Chop Chop" could reach the very top of the sport.

Robert Garcia tips Albert Gonzalez to replicate Bam's success

Speaking to The Ring, Garcia made it clear just how far he believes "Chop Chop" can go:

"I see Chop replicating the same levels of success as Bam, one hundred percent."

"Chop has the same level of hunger and talent as Bam has. Chop wants more and more every time, and he never gives up. He's always first in the gym, and the last one out. He's competitive to be the best at everything. They are both very similar in their approach and how bad they want it.

"Chop is very dedicated and disciplined and is always going to be in great shape for his fights. That's a big plus. And once he gets inside the ring, he's action-packed and combines an accumulation of punches very well. You can't predict what's coming because he puts everything together. It's always something different," added Garcia.

"A lot of trainers have only one fighter, and they can't build another one," Garcia said. "I have a great team around me, and we're going to keep going. I have 15-year-olds right now who are as good and can be even better.

"But first we have to take care of business against Vazquez. It's a tough fight against an experienced fighter, and Chop has to perform. After this next fight, he's ready for any of the champions. We're ready to fight whomever. We don't want an easy route. I know how Top Rank works, and I trust them. If they say we need a couple of more fights, I'm okay with that. I believe he's ready for anyone and can beat any of the champions."

For anyone who has watched "Chop Chop", it's easy to see why he is so highly regarded by many.

He times his shots impressively and doesn't rush his work. He's adept at fighting at range or throwing at volume on the inside. "Chop Chop" is a brilliant body puncher, which, combined with his tight defence on the inside, makes him a fearsome opponent for anyone. He's capable of slipping a punch and landing a brutal shot of his own in return.

We like what we've seen so far, and with the ability he has and having Robert Garcia in his corner, the sky really is the limit for Albert "Chop Chop" Gonzalez.

articles.title: Falcons' throwback social media logo goes viral as fans compare it to Nazi-era imagery
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are facing criticism after revealing a new throwback logo design on social media, with fans spotting a disturbing resemblance.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons' new profile photo on X , which features the Falcons ' logo from the 1960s and 1970s over a black and red background, has drawn quite the reaction – the post revealing the new picture has been viewed more than 15 million times since it was posted Wednesday, Oct. 21.

The post's caption read, "new PFP (profile picture)," followed by an eyeball emoji.

Observers have compared the photo to Nazi imagery, specifically the black and red color scheme and the bird-like image. The Nazi Eagle was a visible part of the German Nazi Party's imagery starting in the 1920s, depicted as a spread-winged eagle holding a wreath and swastika. It is associated closely with antisemitism following the rise of Adolf Hitler and the Holocaust, in which Hitler's Nazi Party murdered an estimated 6 million Jewish people between 1933 and the end of World War II in 1945.

However, Atlanta is wearing 1966-inspired uniforms for its Sunday, Oct. 25, matchup against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers (6-0), according to FOX5 Atlanta . Photos from practice appeared to show the old logo on the red helmets of players; they will also wear a black jersey and white pants.

The Falcons had no comment when reached by USA TODAY Sports.

articles.title: Texas A&M at No. 13 Alabama: Five things to watch against the Tide
articles.summary: Can Texas A&M stun No. 13 Alabama on Saturday? Here are five things to watch in the Week 8 road showdown against the Tide.
articles.body:
Texas A&M football is seeking its first road win over Alabama since 2012 , as the Aggies travel to Tuscaloosa to take on the Crimson Tide on Saturday.

It has been 328 days since Mike Elko's squad recorded a touchdown against a ranked opponent, dating back to the Lone Star Showdown against the Texas Longhorns last year. That is something the Aggies are looking to change against the 13th-ranked Tide in Bryant-Denny Stadium in Week 8.

Texas A&M is coming off its second shutout of the season, a 41-0 rout of The Citadel, while Alabama suffered a 26-10 upset loss to Tennessee last week. If Elko and company want to dethrone the Crimson Tide, they will need sharp quarterback play and to set the tone in the trenches.

Here are five things to watch in Texas A&M's road showdown against Alabama on Saturday:

How will Marcel Reed handle the intimidating road environment?

The junior from Nashville, Tennessee, enters Saturday's contest against the Crimson Tide as Texas A&M's starting quarterback with a 5-5 road record. In those games, Reed has thrown 10 interceptions, averaging one per road game. This season, he has thrown three interceptions in the Aggies' road losses to LSU and Missouri.

Texas A&M can't afford for Reed's inconsistencies to continue against an Alabama defense that has forced 10 interceptions through the first seven weeks. While the Tide are allowing 230.9 passing yards per contest, Reed could be without his star wide receiver Mario Craver, who was listed as "questionable" for the second week in a row in the initial SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report .

Can Texas A&M's defensive line make Keelon Russell feel the heat?

Tennessee lived in the backfield in last week's win over Alabama. The Vols recorded five sacks and forced two interceptions from Russell, punishing the Tide's offensive line. To keep a dangerous dual-threat quarterback like Russell from creating explosive plays, the Aggies must find ways to apply pressure, something Mike Elko's defensive unit has struggled to do in 2026.

Texas A&M ranks at the bottom of the conference with just 5.0 sacks, averaging less than 1.0 sack per game. Defensive coordinator Lyle Hemphill's group is also battling injuries, with starting defensive tackle DJ Hicks and EDGE Anto Saka listed as "questionable" against the Crimson Tide.

Can the Aggie wideouts spark offensive success against Alabama's secondary?

Despite Craver's status for Saturday's showdown, Texas A&M's offense has some young wide receivers emerging in recent weeks. Sophomore TK Norman and freshman Aaron Gregory combined for 182 yards and two touchdowns in the 41-0 shutout of The Citadel last week, showcasing their ability to stretch the field and create space using their speed.

Alabama's secondary has allowed the second-most explosive passing plays in the SEC thus far, which will play an integral role in the Aggies' offensive success.

Will Texas A&M's offensive line establish dominance up front to set up the ground game for success?

The Vols dominated the trenches and paved the way for DeSean Bishop to roll for 159 yards and two touchdowns against the Tide's rush defense, which has been excellent for the majority of the 2026 season. Alabama's defense ranks No. 6 in the SEC, allowing just 107.0 rushing yards per contest entering Saturday's matchup against Texas A&M.

However, the Aggies have two running backs, true freshman KJ Edwards and senior Rueben Owens II, who have eclipsed 300 rushing yards this season and a third, sophomore Jamarion Morrow, who has recorded 122 yards on the ground and leads the room with four touchdowns, despite missing three games due to injury. If Texas A&M's offensive line can establish dominance in the trenches, like Tennessee, it could open up the playcalling and force Alabama to respect the run.

How will the Aggie secondary perform against Russell and Alabama's talented wide receivers?

Ryan Coleman-Williams won't play this weekend, but Alabama has other wideouts who can create explosive plays on a dime. That includes sophomore Lotzeir Brooks, who has burst onto the scene and leads the Tide with 415 receiving yards.

After a slow start to the 2026 campaign, the Aggies' secondary has consistently improved each week. The unit ranks No. 3 in the league, allowing just 164.1 passing yards per game. The unit must be sharp and prevent talent like Brooks from torching them for big gains.

articles.title: Clark girls water polo set to take on Hebron in first state tournament appearance
articles.summary: The Cougars reached the UIL state tournament for the first time in program history and will face water polo power Lewisville Hebron in the state semifinals.
articles.body:
After watching her older sister pick up club water polo, Colette Dreher decided to follow in her sibling's footseteps.

Now, Dreher has reached a level of competition her sister, Lilly, a former Clark water polo team captain, dreamt of - the state tournament.

"This has been years in the making," she said Thursday morning.

Clark girls water polo is making its first UIL state tournament appearance in program history this Friday. Clark (26-3) faces Lewisville Hebron (26-0) in a 10 a.m. state semifinal match at Josh Davis Natatorium. The winner plays Clute Brazoswood or Richmond Foster in Saturday morning's state title match.

"There's a lot of nerves, especially because it's gonna be a really big game," freshman defender Maddie Halliburton said. "But I'm actually just really excited that we got all this far."

In the boys tournament, Boerne Champion is representing the Greater San Antonio area. Boerne Champion (25-3) faces League City Clear Creek (32-3-1) at 1:30 p.m. Friday afternoon in the state semifinals. The winner plays Austin Westlake or Hebron in the boys state finals at noon Saturday. Boerne Champion's boys team has qualified for the state tournament for five straight seasons.

Clark's match against Hebron on Friday will be the second time Clark takes on the Hawks this season. The two teams faced off in a mid-August tournament that resulted in a 11-4 Hebron victory.

"We were just trying to get the groove of everything," junior Ali Maldonado said of the early season match against Hebron. "I think this time is going to be a lot different than before. We were all trying to figure out who we were as players and trying to figure out the team and trying to figure out each other."

But at this point in the season, Clark has the identity it was working to develop in August.

"We have a lot more chemistry now," Clark assistant coach Rebecca Halliburton said. "We're really playing to our strengths. We know what they have. We know this is not going to be an easy battle, but we're prepared."

Dreher usually keys in on the other team's top defenders to allow Maldonado and Halliburton to operate on offense.

"It's my job as the third component to be the defender on their best player," Dreher said. "Just kind of stick to them the whole game."

The trio has been critical to Clark's success so far this season. Statistically, Maldonado leads the team in scoring with 113 goals and Dreher is the team's assists leader with 54.

When Clark took down Harlan 14-13 in the regional final last weekend to qualify for state, Halliburton scored a team-high seven goals, including the game winner. She also leads the team in steals with 116 this season.

"We have such good chemistry," Maldonado said. "And I think that's why we are such a strong team in the water and outside of the water."

Dreher believes surviving the close Harlan match only brought the team closer together. Halliburton's game-winner came at the 2:35 mark in the final period, and the Clark defense prevented Harlan from taking a final shot as time expired.

"That game we didn't let it slip, and if anything, we let it bring us closer together," Dreher said. "I think that does make us more confident for the Hebron game."

While Clark will have to go through a familiar opponent to become the first San Antonio area girls water polo team to win a UIL championship, the Cougars' belief in each other has already led them to make school history.

"It's always been a thought in the back of our mind," Maldonado said of making state. "But we just knew that we had to just go game by game, and we knew that we could make it this far."
